learningObjectives.title: Types of motion and mechanical advantage

questions.q: Which type of motion describes movement back and forth in a straight line?
questions.explain: Reciprocating motion is repeated straight-line movement back and forth, such as a piston in a cylinder.

questions.q: A wheel spinning on an axle is an example of which type of motion?
questions.explain: Rotary motion is movement in a circle around a fixed point or axis.

questions.q: A pendulum swinging back and forth along a curved arc is best described as which type of motion?
questions.explain: Oscillating motion is a swinging movement back and forth along a curved path or arc.

questions.q: In a first-class lever, where is the fulcrum (pivot) located?
options: Between the effort and the load
At the same point as the load
Beyond both the effort and the load
At the same point as the effort
questions.explain: In a first-class lever, such as a seesaw or scissors, the fulcrum sits between the effort and the load.

questions.q: A wheelbarrow is a common example of which class of lever?
questions.explain: In a second-class lever the load lies between the fulcrum and the effort, as in a wheelbarrow.

questions.q: A pair of tweezers is an example of which class of lever?
questions.explain: In a third-class lever the effort is applied between the fulcrum and the load, as with tweezers.

questions.q: Through what angle does a bell crank linkage typically change the direction of motion?
questions.explain: A bell crank changes the direction of motion, usually through 90 degrees, by pivoting about a fixed point.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of an idler gear in a gear train?
options: To reverse the direction of rotation of the output gear
To convert rotary motion into linear motion
questions.explain: An idler gear reverses the output's direction of rotation without altering the overall gear ratio.

questions.q: A cam and follower mechanism converts rotary motion into which type of motion?
options: Rotary motion in the opposite direction
questions.explain: As the cam rotates, the follower rises and falls, producing reciprocating motion.

questions.q: Which formula correctly gives the mechanical advantage of a machine?
questions.explain: Mechanical advantage is the ratio of load to effort, so MA = Load ÷ Effort.

questions.q: When two spur gears mesh together directly, how do they rotate relative to each other?
options: At the same speed regardless of size
questions.explain: Two directly meshing gears always turn in opposite directions.

questions.q: In a belt and pulley system, how can the output speed be reduced compared with the input?
options: Make the driven pulley smaller than the driver pulley
Make the driven pulley larger than the driver pulley
Make both pulleys the same size
questions.explain: A larger driven pulley turns more slowly than a smaller driver pulley, reducing output speed.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a worm and worm wheel mechanism?
options: It gives a small speed reduction and drives in a straight line
It gives a large speed reduction and transmits drive through 90 degrees
It increases output speed and reverses direction
It converts reciprocating motion into rotary motion
questions.explain: A worm and worm wheel produces a large speed reduction and turns the drive through 90 degrees.

questions.q: How is the gear ratio of a pair of meshing gears calculated?
options: Number of teeth on driver ÷ number of teeth on driven
Number of teeth on driven ÷ number of teeth on driver
questions.explain: Gear ratio is found by dividing the number of teeth on the driven gear by the number on the driver gear.

questions.q: Which equation correctly expresses the law of the lever in balance (the principle of moments)?
options: Effort + effort distance = load + load distance
Effort × effort distance = load × load distance
Effort ÷ effort distance = load ÷ load distance
questions.explain: A lever balances when the effort multiplied by its distance equals the load multiplied by its distance from the fulcrum.

questions.q: A driver gear has 20 teeth and meshes with a driven gear of 60 teeth. What is the gear ratio?
questions.explain: Gear ratio = driven ÷ driver = 60 ÷ 20 = 3, giving a ratio of 3:1.

questions.q: A driver gear of 40 teeth turns at 100 rpm and meshes with a driven gear of 20 teeth. What is the output speed of the driven gear?
questions.explain: Output speed = input × (driver teeth ÷ driven teeth) = 100 × (40 ÷ 20) = 200 rpm.

questions.q: On a lever, a load of 200 N acts 0.5 m from the fulcrum. What effort is needed 2 m from the fulcrum to balance it?
questions.explain: Using moments: effort = (200 × 0.5) ÷ 2 = 50 N.

questions.q: A machine lifts a load of 200 N using an effort of 50 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
questions.explain: Mechanical advantage = Load ÷ Effort = 200 ÷ 50 = 4.

questions.q: A rack and pinion mechanism is used to convert which motion into which?
questions.explain: A rotating pinion meshes with a toothed rack, converting rotary motion into straight-line linear motion.
